# 13. Self-Awareness {.unnumbered}

*What is my self-awareness type?*

## The Mindset(s) {.unnumbered}

**Dr. Tasha Eurich** conceptualized this self-awareness model and its four types, based on a
large-scale research program reported in *Insight* (2017) and in the *Harvard Business
Review* (Eurich, 2018). Her team found that self-awareness splits into two dimensions that are
**largely unrelated to each other**: being high on one says almost nothing about the other.
Most people believe they are self-aware; Eurich estimates only **10 to 15%** actually meet the
criteria.

- [**Internal self-awareness**]{style="color:#007F85;"}: how clearly you see your own values,
  passions, aspirations, reactions, strengths and weaknesses, and your impact on others.
  - *Survey item:* items pending.
- [**External self-awareness**]{style="color:#C0522A;"}: how well you understand the way
  other people actually see you, on those same factors.
  - *Survey item:* items pending.

**Polarity:** Internal ↔ External self-awareness.

**Measure:** Self-Reflection & Insight Scale · Insight (Grant, Franklin & Langford, 2002) for
the internal dimension; MCA · Fostering Independence (Fleming et al., 2013). Eurich's model is
a **framework**, not a published self-report scale, so the external dimension still needs a
sourced instrument.

## Your Type {.unnumbered}

Crossing the two dimensions gives Eurich's four self-awareness types. As in Week 1, the useful
move is not picking a side but raising both:

| | **Low External** | **High External** |
|---|---|---|
| **High Internal** | **Introspectors:** clear on who they are, but they do not challenge their own views or seek feedback, so blind spots persist. | **Aware:** know who they are and what they want, and actively seek and value how others see them. |
| **Low Internal** | **Seekers:** do not yet know who they are, what they stand for, or how their team sees them. Often feel stuck or frustrated. | **Pleasers:** so focused on how they come across that they lose track of what matters to them, and drift into choices that do not serve them. |

::: {.callout-note}
## Measure pending
The MCA · Fostering Independence items are already collected at Kickoff. The SRIS · Insight

## Reflect and Plan

::: {.callout-warning}
## Journal
- **Score:** Which of the four types best describes you right now, and what would move you toward Aware?
- **Behavior:** To be the best mentor you can be, what is one new thing you will try to do this week for mentees and/or your team?
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## UGPM Meeting
Both dimensions are trainable, and they are trained differently. Internal self-awareness grows
through better introspection. Eurich's research found that asking **"what"** rather than
**"why"** is what makes introspection productive: "why" invites rationalizing, "what" points
at something you can act on. External self-awareness grows only by asking people who will tell
you the truth.
:::
